difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own proposition prop:transitivity at source lines 842-846 (with the optional title Transitivity): if Gamma proves A and {A} together with Delta proves B, then Gamma together with Delta proves B. The proof at source lines 848-863 is not a one-line invocation of a stated rule. It has to unpack what a derivation from a set of hypotheses is, note that the intermediate steps of the second derivation which depend on the hypothesis A are justified by rules referring to a prior line equal to A, and then manufacture a single derivation of B from Gamma union Delta by concatenating the two derivations and re-justifying exactly those steps by the same rules now applied to the copy of A that comes from the first derivation. The concatenation is a genuine construction: the two derivations have unrelated lengths and the replacement must be made at every line that cited A. No result outside the retained text is used beyond the definition of a derivation.
